questions.question: Find the slope of a line passing through (-1, 2) and (3, 10).
steps: 1. Apply slope formula: m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁).
questions.fastStrategy: Rise over run: (change in y) / (change in x).

questions.question: What is the slope of a horizontal line?
questions.explanation: Horizontal line has no change in y (Δy = 0), so slope = 0 / Δx = 0.
questions.fastStrategy: Horizontal line: slope = 0. Vertical line: slope = undefined.

questions.question: What is the slope of a vertical line?
questions.explanation: Vertical line has no change in x (Δx = 0), so slope = Δy / 0 = undefined.

questions.question: Two lines have slopes m₁ = 2 and m₂ = 1/2. Are they parallel?

choices.E: Yes, they are the same line

questions.explanation: Parallel lines have equal slopes. 2 ≠ 1/2, so not parallel. Perpendicular slopes multiply to -1: 2 × (1/2) = 1 ≠ -1, so not perpendicular.
questions.fastStrategy: Parallel: equal slopes. Perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = -1.
